prs.body:
## Summary

Four artifact-reader tests rewrite the carrier in place with bytes of the **same size** and then expect `reason: "integrity"`. Carrier identity is checked with `sameRegularFileState` (dev, ino, size, mode, mtime/ctime). On filesystems whose timestamps advance in coarse ticks (for example ext4 on Linux 6.12, where two writes a few milliseconds apart get identical `mtimeNs`/`ctimeNs`), the rewrite is invisible to that check, so the tests fail or flake depending on how fast the reader runs. No issue is linked; this is a test-reliability fix found while running targeted suites.

## Problem and expected behavior

Smallest trigger: on Linux 6.12.113 / ext4, Node 24.22.1:

```js
await writeFile(p, Buffer.alloc(1024, 1)); const a = await stat(p, { bigint: true });
await writeFile(p, Buffer.alloc(1024, 2)); const b = await stat(p, { bigint: true });
a.mtimeNs === b.mtimeNs // true on some runs
```

Affected tests on `main` (a01674377):

- `Uf2ArtifactReader.test.ts` › rejects a forged region entry and a changed carrier (fails every run here: `promise resolved "Readable{…}" instead of rejecting`)
- `NodeSeaArtifactReader.test.ts` › rejects post-classification carrier mutation before publishing Node SEA facts: valid replacement / malformed blob (1–2 of 2 fail per run)
- `deno/DenoStandaloneArtifactReader.boundaries.test.ts` › rejects carrier mutation between physical member reads (intermittent)
- `pyinstaller/PyInstallerBoundaries.test.ts` › binds materialization to the inventoried digest and checks cached carrier freshness (intermittent; `"first"` and `"other"` have the same length)

Expected: these tests verify that a changed carrier is rejected, independent of host timestamp granularity.

## Change and scope

Test-only. Each test now records the carrier's stats before the same-size rewrite and afterwards moves `mtime` forward by one second with `utimes` (or `FileHandle.utimes` inside the Deno read hook). This follows the existing pattern in `tests/boundary/filesystem/directoryArtifactReaderOpen.test.ts`. The tests still exercise the real identity check; they just make the mutation observable to it on every filesystem.

Intentionally not included: no production change to `sameRegularFileState` or `ArtifactFileSource`. Detecting same-size, same-tick rewrites would need content rehashing on every open, which is a design decision for maintainers, not a test fix.

prs.title: feat(artifacts): inventory and extract UF2 and DfuSe firmware containers
prs.body:
## Summary

REA cannot read the two drag-and-drop and DFU update containers that most microcontroller firmware ships in. UF2 is the format of the RP2040 and RP2350 bootloaders, of TinyUF2 on ESP32-S2 and ESP32-S3, of LibreTiny's module builds, and of `esptool merge-bin --format uf2`. DfuSe (`.dfu`) is ST's DFU update container. `open_binary` refuses both as an unsupported format, so an analyst cannot see which bytes such a file writes to which addresses.

This PR adds two artifact formats, `uf2` and `dfuse`, to the existing `inspect_artifact` and `extract_artifact` tools. They follow the region model that #7136 landed for Intel HEX and S-record: each address-contiguous region is an extractable inventory entry with region metadata. A DfuSe suffix CRC mismatch follows the existing `integrity_policy`.

Part of the embedded roadmap #7955. Refs #7478 (the format vocabularies this PR extends).

## Problem and expected behavior

- Before: on `main` (`d48e472fa`), `rea inspect-artifact <file> --json` on an esptool v4.12.0 `merge_bin --format uf2` output, and on a two-target DfuSe file, both exit 1 with `"code": "target_unavailable"`, `"category": "unsupported_target"`, "Cannot open artifact: unsupported binary format." and `"constraint": "file_format_rejected"`.
- After: the UF2 file opens as a `uf2` archive with one region per familyID and address range; the DfuSe file opens as a `dfuse` archive with one region per element. Extraction writes each region's bytes.

## Change and scope

- **Domain** (`src/domain/firmware/`, pure and `Result`-based): `uf2.ts` joins valid main-flash block payloads into address-contiguous regions per familyID and counts block numbering. `dfuse.ts` parses the prefix, targets, elements and DFU suffix, and computes the suffix CRC. `uf2Families.ts` names 32 family IDs from microsoft/uf2 `utils/uf2families.json` at `cf3bd7f9` (MIT; notice preserved), including 8 that LibreTiny builds for; other IDs keep their value only. `addressRuns.ts` and `regionDecoder.ts` replace HEX's private run merging and failure types.
- **Reader**: `DecodedRegionArtifactReader` takes over the retained-region plumbing that `HexRecordArtifactReader` owned (streams, cancellation, close, carrier identity). HEX, UF2 and DfuSe readers are thin subclasses with format adapters.
- **Format registry** (#8054): both formats get the HEX capabilities and one reader limitation each.
- **Recognition** is by strong magic only, after HEX and S-record and before ESP images and FIT. UF2 needs a complete first block with all three magic numbers. DfuSe needs the version 1 `DfuSe` prefix and a DFU 1.1a suffix; the CRC is not part of recognition, and classification reads the file's last 16 bytes.
- **UF2 regions** are `family-0x<id>/0x<start>-0x<end>.bin`, one address space per family. Out-of-order blocks are sorted, identical rewrites count as `duplicate_bytes`, and a conflicting rewrite fails the file, as in HEX. Invalid, partial, not-main-flash and file-container blocks are excluded and reported; MD5 and extension-tag blocks are counted, not decoded. Numbering is grouped by familyID and block count, and each block number records the addresses it was seen at, because esptool numbers each merged input from 0. Missing or ambiguous numbering makes coverage unknown.
- **DfuSe regions** are `target-<t>/element-<e>-0x<start>-0x<end>.bin`: one entry per element at its file range, with its target's alternate setting and name. Overlaps within one alternate setting are named, and structural faults fail with a byte offset. `DFUImageSize` may include the suffix or not, because producers disagree. `compare_artifacts` treats the alternate setting and target name as a declaration, so the same bytes moved to another device memory are `changed`.
- **Integrity**: a CRC mismatch follows `integrity_policy`. `fail` refuses with `artifact_integrity_mismatch` (`algorithm: "dfu-crc32"`); `record-and-continue` marks the root `mismatched` with a `dfu-crc32` contradiction that extraction carries.
- **Limits**: 128 MiB per file, as for HEX (#6176 tracks configurable ceilings); at most 65,536 UF2 regions and 65,536 DfuSe elements with bytes.
- **Docs**: `docs/uf2-dfuse.md`, linked from the existing guides and the skill; the lane in `docs/testing.md`; container contradictions in `docs/mcp-contracts.md`; notices for the family names.
- **Not included**: MD5 region checks, extension tags, UF2 file-container reconstruction, plain DFU suffix files, CRC checks for nested DfuSe files, and raw-binary or Ghidra loading of regions.

Deliberate choices reviewers may question:

- **Invalid UF2 blocks are excluded, not fatal**, because each block carries its own framing and address. A malformed HEX record still fails its file.
- **The UF2 MD5 structure is not verified.** It describes device flash for a flasher, not the block's file bytes, and esptool v4.12.0 and v5.6.0 do not place it where the specification says.
- **The root carries no `declared_integrity`**, which holds entry digests; the DFU CRC lives in the contradiction and in `format_metadata`.
- **`family_name` is an REA label**; `family_id` is the fact, and the root records `family_name_registry`.

Contribution scope: reads local files only, inside the existing artifact tools; no execution, injection, mutation or protection recovery. Not applicable.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: `uf2.ts` and `dfuse.ts` own recognition and decoding; `artifactFormats.ts` owns both formats' capabilities; `scanReader.ts` applies the integrity policy to a reader's `containerIntegrity()`. Resolution, classification, inventory, extraction, inspection and comparison consume them. Superseded: HEX's private stream and merge code and four identical failure types.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: not applicable.
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: format values `uf2` and `dfuse`; `format_metadata` kinds `uf2`, `uf2-region`, `dfuse` and `dfuse-element`; a `dfu-crc32` variant in the inventory and inspection contradiction schemas and the `artifact_integrity_mismatch` details (`docs/error-contract.schema.json` regenerated). No new inputs. Against `d48e472fa`, `tools/list` grows by 16,998 bytes (+0.44%) in the default profile and 17,586 bytes (+0.39%) with full input schemas, almost all in output schemas; by 14 bytes with compact output schemas.
- Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility: two new archive target formats; no provider is involved.
- Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract: Evidence, snapshots and bundles can carry the new values, which older REA versions cannot parse (closed enums and unions; derived from the source). **Compatibility decision requested:** CONTRIBUTING.md requires an explicit decision for persisted formats. Please decide whether this addition is acceptable as is and whether it needs a release note.
- Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details: files that pass recognition, which `open_binary` refused, now resolve as `uf2` or `dfuse` archives.
- Generated metadata (`docs/public/product-catalog.json`), package, or installation impact: none. New optional `npm run verify:uf2` lane.

**Real tools.** `npm run verify:uf2` ran on `df4154b4c` with esptool v4.12.0 (the ESP-IDF v5.5.2 environment) and with v5.6.0, on macOS. It builds UF2 files with esptool `merge-bin --format uf2` from inputs at known addresses. ## Problem and expected behavior

A headerless ARM7 firmware image could be analyzed by Ghidra directly but was rejected by REA's Windows target admission. Common firmware carriers also need address-aware parsing before their payloads can be analyzed. The new workflows report supported structures, payload identities and explicit coverage limits rather than treating every `.bin` as executable code.

prs.title: feat(artifacts): inventory and extract Android boot and vendor_boot images
prs.body:
## Summary

Android firmware analysis usually starts with `boot.img`, `init_boot.img`, `recovery.img` or `vendor_boot.img`. REA could not open these images. `inspect-artifact` saw an ordinary file, so the kernel, ramdisk, second stage and devicetree inside stayed out of reach.

This adds a reader that recognizes `ANDROID!` headers in versions 0 to 4 and `VNDRBOOT` headers in versions 3 and 4 by magic, independent of the filename. The stored components become artifact children, so `inspect-artifact`, `extract-artifact` and the `inspect_artifact` MCP tool inventory and extract them through the existing safe output tree. No issue is linked. This is a proposed new artifact format.

## Problem and expected behavior

Use case: an analyst holds a boot or vendor_boot image from a firmware dump and wants its header facts and component bytes without running anything.

Observable outcome:

- `root_format` is `android-boot-image`, with `image_kind` `boot` or `vendor-boot`.
- Root metadata reports header version, page size, header size, OS version and security patch level when present, board name, command line (extra command line folded in for v0 to v2), component sizes, load addresses where the version has them, and the header digest.
- Non-empty components become children: `kernel`, `ramdisk`, `second`, `recovery_dtbo`, `dtb`, the v3 `vendor_ramdisk`, v4 named `vendor_ramdisk/<name>` entries from the ramdisk table, `bootconfig`, and the v4 boot signature.
- gzip, lz4 and zstd payloads are recorded from their leading magic and left compressed.
- An AVB footer is reported as present, with version and sizes only. Nothing is verified.
- The header cannot say whether an `ANDROID!` file is a boot, init_boot or recovery image, so that is stated as a limitation rather than guessed.

## Change and scope

Header parsing lives in `src/domain/androidBootImageFormat.ts`, following AOSP `include/bootimg/bootimg.h` and `mkbootimg.py`. `src/artifacts/AndroidBootImageArtifactReader.ts` maps the parsed layout to children through the stable artifact read. Existing owners change only to register the format: `artifactFormats.ts`, `ArtifactReader.ts`, `inventory/ArtifactGraphConstruction.ts`, `artifactFormatMetadata.ts`, `artifactGraph.ts`, `binaryTargetTypes.ts`, `evidenceSubject.ts`, `analysisSnapshot.ts`, `liveBinaryTargetSummary.ts` and `BinaryTargetResolver.ts`. This is the same registration path the uImage reader used.

Admission is bounded before any table is read: at most 4096 vendor ramdisk entries, a 4096-byte table entry, and a 1 MiB vendor header. Component ranges are checked against the file size, and a truncated or overlapping layout fails closed instead of producing partial children.

Not included: decompressing ramdisks, verifying the AVB footer or v4 signature, or unpacking the kernel. Extracted children can be passed to the existing ELF, kernel and devicetree tools.

Follow the [contribution scope](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-scope).

capabilities involving target execution, injection, mutation, or protection
recovery; ordinary fixes within existing boundaries may state "not applicable".

unchecked. Maintainers can help resolve open questions.

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: new Android boot image parser in `src/domain/` and reader in `src/artifacts/`, registered in the existing artifact format owners.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: read-only inspection and safe extraction of a local artifact, with no target execution, injection, mutation or protection recovery. prs.title: feat(artifacts): inventory IMG v2 archives and ANP3 animation packages
prs.body:
## Summary

`open_binary` refused IMG version 2 archives (`VER2`) and ANP3 animation packages (`ANP3`) with `unsupported binary format`, so `inspect_artifact` and `extract_artifact` could not list their members or animations. Both are asset formats of a legacy game engine: IMG v2 is a sector-based archive container and ANP3 is a keyframed skeletal animation package. They are now recognized by signature and inventoried as stored byte ranges, like Godot PCK and UnityFS. No issue is linked; this is a self-contained format-inspection addition within the existing artifact scope.

## Problem and expected behavior

- An IMG archive lists every directory row as a member with its name, physical offset, size, SHA-256 and declared sector fields. Members can be extracted.
- An ANP3 package lists every animation with its object count, bones (name, id, frame type, keyframe count), keyframe count and duration.
- An ANP3 member of an IMG archive is classified as `anp3` by its bytes, and inspection suggests extracting it for separate inspection.

## Change and scope

- `src/domain/imgArchiveFormat.ts`: pure `VER2` header/directory parser. Size is the archive size, or the streaming size when it is 0 (as shipped archives are written). A directory that cannot fit, a member outside the file or starting inside the directory, and an empty, unterminated or multi-component name fail as malformed instead of being repaired.
- `src/domain/anp3AnimationFormat.ts`: pure ANP3 parser. Frame types 1–4 (20/32/10/16 bytes). Keyframes are skipped except each object's final time; duration is the latest final time, `null` without keyframes or with a non-finite float time (reported as a limitation). Truncation and unknown frame types fail with the byte offset. Trailing bytes (IMG sector padding) are reported, not refused.
- `src/artifacts/ImgAnp3ArtifactReader.ts`: one `PositionalArtifactReader` subclass for both formats; it owns only the layout reads. IMG directories are bounded before decoding (65,536 rows under the 64 MiB retained-metadata budget) and aliased rows are charged against the shared expansion budget. ANP3 packages are parsed in memory with a fixed 16 MiB ceiling (shipped packages are a few MiB).
- Format ids `img-v2` / `anp3` and metadata kinds `img-v2`, `img-v2-entry`, `anp3`, `anp3-animation` are wired through the same vocabularies as UF2/DfuSe. All four metadata kinds are `notCompared` in artifact comparison: their facts come from bytes that content comparison already covers, or are layout.
- Docs: new `docs/img-anp3-artifacts.md`, CLI guide, index, VitePress nav, and the skill reference.

Not included: IMG version 1 (headerless `.img` + `.dir`), IMG version 3, the earlier ANPK/ANP2 animation layouts, decoding of model/texture/collision streams stored as IMG members, keyframe value decoding, and in-place expansion of nested members (inventory expands only ASAR today; nested ANP3 members are classified and reachable through extraction).

Contribution scope fit: format inspection and ordinary archive extraction; no maintainer scope decision needed ("not applicable").

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: the two domain parsers own all interpretation; `ImgAnp3ArtifactReader` consumes their parsed rows and records. No superseded path.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: not applicable (read-only format inspection).
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: additive enum values for artifact/target formats and four new `format_metadata` kinds; `inspect_artifact` may return a new `extract_artifact` next probe for IMG archives with ANP3 members.
- Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility: new target formats only; no provider involved.
- Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract: occurrences keep physical offsets and verified hashes; coverage is complete with the sector-padding limitation for IMG.
- Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details: reuses the admitted descriptor, identity rechecks and stream retirement of `PositionalArtifactReader`.
- Generated metadata, package, or installation impact: none committed; `docs:check` passes.

Expected effects:

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.
- [ ] Launch or attach to a process.

prs.body:
## Summary

Real-tool verifiers each wrote their own fixture-root lifecycle. Several removed the root after a failed MCP client or transport close, or before the child that used the root had exited. This PR adds one owner, `VerifierFixture` (`scripts/lib/verifier-fixture.mjs`), built on `src/process`'s `PrivateRuntimeRoot`. It moves the seven verifiers that had partial or wrong ordering onto it, deletes the two helpers it replaces, and adds a counted guard so new verifiers allocate roots through the owner.

Refs #322, #328 (real-Windows verifiers that should build their fixture roots on this owner; both still need a real non-admin Windows run). #4396 is not addressed: it asks for negative controls in reconstruction obligation ledgers, which is unrelated to fixture lifecycle (the audit's S22 grouping put it here). #8559 (native UI ready handshake) stays deferred because it needs a real macOS GUI run.

## Problem and expected behavior

S22 in the structural audit lists 18 verifier-ownership issues (#8552, #8555, #8561, #8562, #8564, #8595, #10311, among others). Each was fixed one at a time in its own script. The underlying cause stayed: every `scripts/verify-*.mjs` allocated a root with `mkdtemp` and removed it in its own `finally`. One trigger that is still on main: `scripts/verify-apk-signature.mjs` removes its workspace even when `client.close()` or `transport.close()` failed, so the MCP server child may still be using it.

Expected invariant: a fixture root is removed only after every resource that may still use it (MCP clients and transports, sessions, sentinels, process-lineage checks) has confirmed cleanup. Otherwise the root is retained, the failure names its path, and the failure carries a handle that can retry the release.

## Change and scope

Design:

- `VerifierFixture.open({ prefix, parent })` allocates a `PrivateRuntimeRoot` (owner-only `mkdtemp` on POSIX, the native DACL root on Windows). `new VerifierFixture({ path, close })` adopts a root that is already allocated. `private: false` allocates a plain temporary directory for child scratch space: on Windows a private root keeps a DELETE handle that stops children from creating temporary directories beneath it (the WABT verifier's existing constraint).
- `fixture.releaseAfter(cleanup)` registers something that must confirm before the root may go. Registration closes when the first release starts and stays closed after a failed attempt.
- `fixture.release()` runs pending cleanups in registration order, attempting every one and keeping each failure. It removes the root only when all have confirmed. On failure it throws `AggregateError` with the cleanup failures plus a "Retained verifier fixture <path>" error, and sets `cleanupLeases: [fixture]`, the same retry contract the removed `withVerifierWorkspace` exposed. A retry runs only the cleanups that have not confirmed, then the root. Concurrent releases share one attempt.
- `withVerifierFixture(fixture, operation)` keeps both the verification failure and the cleanup failure (through the existing `withVerifierCleanup`). When the fixture is retained, the caught failure carries `cleanupLeases: [fixture]`.
- `onceConfirmed(cleanup)` shares one cleanup between fixtures that both depend on it (WABT's two roots and their one MCP client). A confirmed attempt is not repeated, and a failed one is retried.

Migrated: `verify-recorded-crash`, `verify-signal-recording`, `verify-wasm-artifact` (previously `releaseAfter`), `verify/firmware/{esp-flash,esp-image,uf2-esptool}` (previously `withVerifierWorkspace`), and `verify-apk-signature` (previously removed the root after a failed close). Removed: `releaseAfter` from `verifier-cleanup.mjs`, all of `verifier-workspace.mjs`, and their tests, which are replaced by `tests/process-global/verifierFixture.test.ts`.

Guard: `scripts/verify/architecture-guards.mjs` counts root allocations (`mkdtemp`, `mkdtempSync`, `createCanonicalTemporaryDirectory`, `PrivateRuntimeRoot.create`) in `scripts/verify-*.mjs` and `scripts/verify/**`. The baseline (`verifier-fixture-root`, 97 files, 102 sites) can only shrink.

Not included: migrating the remaining 97 verifiers. They will move in further slices, and the guard stops new copies meanwhile. Also not included: the native UI verifier (#8559), and any change to `src/` runtime behavior. Behavior change: in the WABT verifier, a leaked provider workspace now keeps the child temp root for diagnosis instead of removing it.

Contribution scope: not applicable (verification scripts only, within existing boundaries).

prs.title: fix(artifacts): decide how compare_artifacts compares every format_metadata kind
prs.body:
Part of the embedded roadmap #7955.

## Summary

`compare_artifacts` compares some `format_metadata` declarations. On `main`, the compared kinds are named by hand in six per-format functions and fields, so a new kind goes uncompared and nothing reports it. ESP segment load addresses were first missed this way, and UnityFS member flags still are. This PR puts the decision in one table beside the schemas. Each kind either projects the declaration that comparison compares or states why comparison uses none of its facts, and a kind without an entry does not compile. A conformance test checks that the contract names exactly the compared kinds.

## Problem and expected behavior

| Case | `main` `d48e472fa` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A node-less PYZ namespace record becomes encrypted | unchanged | `changed` `[metadata]` |
| A PyInstaller member's declaration changes while its bytes are unavailable, for example a link name stored as NFC, then NFD | `unknown` `[metadata, availability]` | `changed` `[metadata, availability]` |
| A UnityFS member's raw `flags` change, with equal bytes | unchanged | `changed` `[metadata]` |
| Only one side records a compared declaration | a Node SEA sentence for Node SEA; no limitation for ESP segments, FIT images or PyInstaller entries | one generic limitation for every compared kind |
| A symlink in a POSIX directory, app bundle or DMG inventory | `executable` from the link's own mode bits (Linux reports 0777 for every symlink) | never `executable` |
| Declared digests of one algorithm differ, and either side has no content | `unknown` `[availability]` | `unknown` `[metadata, availability]` |

The first four rows were executed on `main` with hand-built inventories (see Evidence). The last two are derived from source, and so are row 4's FIT and PyInstaller cases.

On `main`, `declarationChanged` makes a path without content `changed` when ASAR storage or a Node SEA, ESP segment, DfuSe element, ESP flash partition or FIT declaration changed, but not a PyInstaller declaration. PyInstaller declaration comparison (`142cf188a`) is older than that exception, and no test or commit gives a reason to leave it out. Here every compared declaration counts, so such a result's status can be `changed` instead of `unknown`. `main`'s sentence in `docs/python-packaged-applications.md`, "Missing declaration facts and unavailable non-metadata content remain unknown.", predates the exception; this PR rewords it.

The generic limitation replaces "Node SEA member metadata is recorded on only one side for matching paths; …" with "Format metadata declarations are missing on one side or differ in kind for matching paths; omitted metadata may be a legacy or non-container observation and leaves the complete declaration unavailable."

Unchanged from `main`: #7932's rule that a path without content is `unknown` unless a declaration changed, FIT per-field unknowns, and the comparison of occurrence limitation text. `dotnet-bundle-entry`, the Bun kinds, `hex-record-region`, `esp-flash-image`, `uf2`, `uf2-region` and `dfuse` stay uncompared, and `esp-flash-partition` and `dfuse-element` compare the same fields as on `main`. A HEX region's path names its start and end addresses, so its declaration could never differ between paired regions.

## Change and scope

- `src/domain/artifactFormatMetadata.ts`: `declarationsByKind` decides all 26 kinds. Compared: `unityfs-entry` (`source_path` and raw `flags`; new), `pyinstaller-entry`, `node-sea-entry`, `esp-image-segment`, `dfuse-element`, `esp-flash-partition` and `fit-image` (with its unreadable fields). Each other kind states why it is not compared. `main`'s six `*Declaration` functions are removed.
- `src/domain/artifactComparison.ts`: `OccurrenceMetadata` holds four comparisons: ASAR storage, encryption, the table's declaration and that declaration's field availability. A declaration changed when ASAR storage or the table's declaration changed. A node-less metadata record compares its declaration, `encrypted`, `executable` and any recorded ASAR storage. Here a node-less record is a `metadata` occurrence without `artifact_id` on both sides, with a compared declaration on at least one side. Its limitations are not compared, as on `main`. A metadata record that has content keeps the content comparison. `classifyPyInstallerDeclaration` and `compareFitImageDeclarations` are removed.
- `src/artifacts/hostExecutableMarking.ts`: a symlink has no executable marking on any host, because running a symlink runs its target.
- Docs: the contract in `docs/mcp-contracts.md`, and the Godot PCK, HEX/S-record, UnityFS and PyInstaller guides.
- Commits, in stack order:
  - the table: `9e65be9e3`, `88869713e`, `3e51a7760` (.NET bundle members stay uncompared, as on `main`) and `7978b9400` (HEX regions too);
  - encryption in `OccurrenceMetadata`: `2b66531c7`;
  - `executable` on records, symlinks and declared digests: `2fc3bd2c1`, `a6e09ece3`, `0c92f1c57`;
  - the docs test and a shared acceptance fixture: `1a068ac21`, `964be7465`;

  The merges of `main` adopt #7932, so some earlier commit messages describe superseded behavior. For example, `2fc3bd2c1` says `changed`, and `9dbf90bd9` stops comparing limitation text; that change is undone. The branch also holds #7498's pre-squash commits. Their content is already in `main`, so they add nothing to the diff.

Limitation text still counts as `metadata`, as on `main`, so a new reader caveat can mark an unchanged member changed: adding ZIP member `A` does this to `a` through its case-collision note.   - `main`'s Fit, UnavailableMetadata, HistoricalSummary and Plist acceptance tests are unchanged and pass.
- Base reproduction or other evidence, executed on `main` `d48e472fa`:
  - This PR's `src/domain/artifactComparison.test.ts` (at `2304a0596`) fails 6 of its 32 tests on `main`'s source:
    - The one-sided and mismatched-kind cases get no limitation.

- `CudaMetadataBudget`, sqlite `OutputBudget`: their field names escape the guard pattern; left for a slice that also widens the pattern.

`Budget` additions:
- `chargeEvicting(amount, evict)`: evicts oldest entries until the charge fits; an amount above the maximum evicts nothing.

prs.title: fix(artifacts): require each reader traversal to declare its coverage
prs.body:
## Summary

Artifact traversal coverage was "complete" unless a reader said otherwise. `ArtifactTraversalObservation` started at `#unknown = false`, and `onCoverage` was optional, so a reader that said nothing was reported as complete. Six readers (ASAR, Bun standalone, .NET bundle, iNES, Mach-O slices, ZIP) never called it, and several others reported nothing on their "nothing to report" path. This PR makes each reader declare its coverage. A traversal that ends without a declaration is now reported as `unknown`, with a limitation that names the reader.

Refs structural audit W6 step 1 (reports 05 §1 and 12 rows 9a/9b).

## Problem and expected behavior

- Trigger: a reader yields its members and returns without calling `onCoverage`. Before this PR, `inventory_artifact`, `extract_artifact`, release exposure, Apple asset-catalog, Interface Builder and executable-root discovery all reported `traversal.status: "complete"` for that traversal.
- Broken rule: completeness is a claim the producer must make. It must not be the default.
- Silence also hid gaps across traversals. One observer can span several traversals, for example an inventory of a directory that contains nested ASAR archives. If one traversal declared complete and another stayed silent, the result was still complete.
- New behavior: each traversal must declare its own coverage. If it does not, it adds `unknown` with `The <format> reader ended its traversal without declaring coverage; members it did not list are unknown.` If its consumer stops it before the reader finishes, it adds `unknown` with `The <format> traversal stopped before the reader finished; …`.

## Change and scope

- `declaredArtifactEntries(reader, signal, sink)` in `ArtifactTraversalObservation.ts` is the single owner of the rule. It wraps one traversal and tracks whether that traversal declared coverage and whether it ran to the end. Its iterator forwards `next` and `return` unchanged, so callers unwind readers exactly as they did before. This preserves the nested-unwind cleanup test in `artifactInventorySnapshot.test.ts`. A failed traversal adds nothing: its failure is the result.
- `ArtifactTraversalObservation` no longer implements `ArtifactTraversalOptions`. Its sinks are renamed `record`/`omit`, and `observation.entries(reader, signal)` runs a traversal through the helper. **Type guard:** `ArtifactTraversalOptions` has only optional members, so it is a weak type. Passing the observation straight to `reader.entries(signal, observation)` is now a compile error ("no properties in common"). The silent bypass cannot come back.
- Readers now declare complete coverage when they have listed everything:
  - **iNES, Mach-O slices, Bun standalone, .NET bundle:** the verification (report 12 §9) found these list everything or throw.
  - **Directory:** declares complete coverage. Unreadable directories and non-UTF-8 names still declare `unknown`.
  - **UnityFS, wxapkg, Deno:** now also declare their available path.
  - **ASAR:** declares complete. The duplicate-member case is fixed separately in #10552 (still open). Until that PR lands, ASAR behaves exactly as it does on main.
  - **ZIP:** declares complete relative to its central directory, which is unchanged from main. A follow-up PR adds byte accounting for local entries that the central directory does not list.
- Producers used "undefined" to mean "complete": `PositionalArtifactEntries.coverage`, `DecodedRegions.coverage`, and Fit's `#coverage`. These fields are now required, and every producer states complete coverage explicitly (Godot PCK, Node SEA, ESP image, ESP flash, Intel HEX/SREC, UF2, DfuSe, Fit). An unprepared reader declares nothing and therefore reads as unknown.
- Consumers that wrap an inner reader now go through the helper, so a silent inner reader cannot be hidden by the outer reader's own declaration. These are the native DMG reader (attached directory) and the desktop application reader.
- `docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md` states the rule.
- ZIP byte accounting follows in #10580, stacked on this PR.
- **Not included:** the `Coverage` domain type and combiner (W6 step 2), `completeWithinViewCoverage(n, n)` callers, and `?? true` defaults. `scanReader` with no reader still returns complete, because a single file has no members.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: each `ArtifactReader` owns its coverage declaration. `declaredArtifactEntries` owns the rule that silence means unknown. The superseded path is consumers passing the observation directly to `reader.entries`.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: not applicable (fix within existing boundaries).
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: no schema change. A traversal that was silently complete is now `unknown` with a limitation. All production readers now declare, so known inputs produce the same output as before.
- Provider, bridge, target-format, or platform compatibility: none.
- Evidence, artifact, provenance, or reconstruction contract: coverage can only become more conservative (`unknown`) when a reader or consumer does not finish its declared traversal.
- Target selection, authority, upstream behavior, and cleanup details: iterator `return` is still forwarded to the reader, so cleanup order is unchanged.
- Generated metadata, package, or installation impact: none.

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- Tests added or updated:

## Summary

`Fixes #9423`

Prefetch files were recognized only by name, so `inspect-artifact` never read the
execution history their header records. Recognize the format from its bytes and
report the header fields a v17 or v23 file actually records, offline.

## Problem and expected behavior

A `.pf` file under any other name stayed a plain file. The expected behavior is
that `inspect_artifact` reports it as root format `windows-prefetch` with its
recorded executable name, name-hash, declared size and run totals, and that
fields this reader does not decode are named as unknown rather than shown empty.

- `src/domain/windows/prefetchFormat.ts` owns recognition and header parsing and
  returns a `Result` failure of kind `format`, `limit` or `unsupported`.
- `WindowsPrefetchArtifactReader` reads the admitted file, parses it, and exposes
  the facts through `formatMetadata()`. The file is its own content, so the root
  occurrence carries every fact and no members are enumerated.
- `windows-prefetch` joins the artifact format id and content-format lists, the
  format registry (a container with `roleContainer`), and the classifier.
